tools.name: apply_patch
tools.description:
Apply a multi-file standard Unified Diff patch in an isolated temporary workspace. Agent mode only.
Binary patches, renames/copies and file mode changes are unsupported and rejected before writing.
Format:
--- a/path/to/existing.ext
+++ b/path/to/existing.ext
@@ -1,3 +1,3 @@
 context
-old line
+new line
--- /dev/null
+++ b/path/to/new_file.ext
@@ -0,0 +1,2 @@
+line1
+line2
--- a/path/to/deleted.ext
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,1 +0,0 @@
-removed line

patch.description: Standard Unified Diff patch text (--- a/file, +++ b/file, @@ -L,C +L,C @@).

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Run a project shell command asynchronously with no default duration limit. Agent mode only. Output is bounded without terminating the job. Use list/status <id>/kill <id> for monitoring and cancellation. Set background=true for persistent servers or watchers; ordinary long builds can remain foreground jobs.

background.description: Set true to start a persistent background server/watcher.

tools.name: debug_clear_breakpoint
tools.description: Remove a source breakpoint at a specific file_path and line number.

file_path.description: Absolute or project-relative path of the source file.

line.description: 1-based line number to clear breakpoint from.

tools.name: debug_continue
tools.description: Resume execution until next breakpoint or termination.

tools.name: debug_disconnect
tools.description: Disconnect from the debug adapter.

tools.name: debug_down
tools.description: Select stack frame down towards callee. Optional count (default 1).

count.description: Number of stack frames to navigate down (default 1).

tools.name: debug_eval
tools.description: Evaluate an expression in the paused frame and return its value. (what the adapter can evaluate depends on the language; see the language profile).

tools.name: debug_get_context
tools.description: Inspect the live debug session: the paused thread's call-stack and all in-scope variables.

tools.name: debug_kill
tools.description: Terminate the debuggee process.

tools.name: debug_list_breakpoints
tools.description: List all source breakpoints (file and line) known to the debugger.

tools.name: debug_modules
tools.description: List loaded modules and shared libraries in target process.

tools.name: debug_pause
tools.description: Pause execution of running debuggee and return paused location, stack, and variables.

tools.name: debug_quit
tools.description: Close only the captured adapter and its owned children, not other Dape sessions.

tools.name: debug_restart
tools.description: Restart the debugging session with current configuration.

tools.name: debug_scope
tools.description: Inspect scopes or expand child variables of a struct/vector by name.

variable_name.description: Name of variable to expand child fields for (e.g. 'frame', 'landmarks_2d').

tools.name: debug_set_breakpoint
tools.description: Set a source breakpoint at a file_path and 1-based line number. Requires both parameters.

file_path.description: Absolute or project-relative path of the source file.

line.description: 1-based line number to set breakpoint on.

tools.name: debug_sources
tools.description: List known source files reported by the debug adapter.

tools.name: debug_stack
tools.description: List call stack frames for the current thread.

tools.name: debug_start
tools.description: Start or attach a Dape debugging session with optional config_name.

tools.name: debug_step_in
tools.description: Step into the function call on the current line.

tools.name: debug_step_out
tools.description: Step out of current function back to caller.

tools.name: debug_step_over
tools.description: Step to the next source line in current function (does not step into calls).

tools.name: debug_threads
tools.description: List all threads reported by the active debugger adapter.

tools.name: debug_toggle_breakpoint
tools.description: Toggle a breakpoint at file_path and line number.

file_path.description: Absolute or project-relative path of the source file.

tools.name: debug_up
tools.description: Select stack frame up towards caller. Optional count (default 1).

count.description: Number of stack frames to navigate up (default 1).

tools.name: debug_watch
tools.description: List or update this chat's watch expressions for the current adapter; independent of Dape's global UI list.

expression.description: Expression to add or remove from watch list.

remove.description: Set true to remove expression instead of adding.

tools.name: edit_by_lsp
tools.description: Replace the entire implementation body or definition of a specific symbol (function, method, class, struct, type) in a source file with new content. Uses exact language-agnostic LSP/imenu symbol line boundaries. ALWAYS PREFER THIS over edit_file for modifying existing code definitions across all programming languages.

file_path.description: Absolute or project-relative path of the file to edit.

symbol.description: Name of the symbol (function, method, class, struct, type) to replace.

new_content.description: New code to replace the entire symbol body/definition with (use empty string to delete).

kind.description: Optional symbol kind filter (e.g. Function, Method, Class, Struct, Type).

tools.name: edit_file
tools.description: Replace an exact unique block in an existing file. Read the relevant lines first, then supply old_string with enough surrounding text to be unique and new_string. Prefer structural editing when available. Changes follow the active review policy and retain rollback snapshots. Verify with available diagnostics and project tests.

file_path.description: Absolute or project-relative path of the file to edit.

old_string.description: The exact unique string to replace, copied from read_file without the line-number prefix.

reason.description: One-sentence justification of the edit, shown to the human during review.

tools.name: find_files
tools.description: Find project files matching a glob pattern (e.g. **/*.rs, *.el, *test*) using bounded native Rust discovery. Includes hidden sources, applies configured directory/artifact exclusions, and reports incomplete searches. Read-only, available in all modes.

tools.name: git_blame
tools.description: Show line-by-line Git commit and author information for a file. Read-only, available in all modes.

end_line.description: Optional end line, defaults to end of file.

tools.name: git_branch
tools.description: Manage Git branches (list, create, switch, delete). Agent mode only.

action.description: Action: list, create, switch, or delete.

tools.name: git_branches
tools.description: List local and remote Git branches. Read-only, available in every mode.

tools.name: git_commit
tools.description: Record staged changes in repository. Agent mode only.

all.description: If true, automatically stage all modified tracked files.

tools.name: git_diff
tools.description: Show Git diff (staged changes with staged:true, unstaged, or specific commit/path). Read-only, available in all modes.

path.description: Optional file or directory path to diff.

tools.name: git_log
tools.description: Show recent Git commit log. Read-only, available in all modes.

path.description: Optional file path to limit history to.

tools.name: git_stage
tools.description: Stage file(s) into git index (git add). Agent mode only.

paths.description: Literal file or directory path to stage (e.g. '.' for all).

tools.name: git_stash
tools.description: Stash changes (push, apply, list). Apply pins the selected object before approval and never deletes it. Pop/drop are refused; delete manually with Git/Magit. Agent mode only.

action.description: Action: push, apply, or list. Pop/drop are unsupported.

stash.description: Required for apply: explicit stash@{N} reference, for example stash@{1}.

tools.name: git_stashes
tools.description: List Git stash entries and their indices. Read-only, available in every mode.

tools.name: git_status
tools.description: Show structured Git repository status (branch, upstream, staged, unstaged, untracked). Magit-style. Read-only, available in all modes.

tools.name: git_unstage
tools.description: Unstage file(s) from git index (git restore --staged). Agent mode only.

tools.name: list_files
tools.description: List a project directory using GNU ls -lAh through the Rust command service. Read-only in all modes; returns ls text with bounded output and explicit truncation. For custom ls options use the bash tool with the full command.

path.description: Directory path to list (default: project root).

tools.name: lsp_diagnostics
tools.description: Get compiler and linter diagnostics (errors, warnings) from LSP via Flymake. Pass 'file_path' to inspect a specific file, or OMIT 'file_path' (pass empty or no arguments) to scan the ENTIRE PROJECT for all compile and lint errors across all project files. Always call this after editing or building to verify zero compilation errors.

file_path.description: Optional. Absolute or project-relative path of a specific file to check. When omitted or empty, runs a project-wide diagnostic scan across all project files.

tools.name: lsp_find_symbol
tools.description: Locate where a named symbol (function, type, variable) is defined in the workspace. Returns file:line for each definition candidate.

symbol_name.description: Name of the symbol to look up, e.g. the function or type name.

tools.name: lsp_project_skeleton
tools.description: Get a compact map of the whole project: every file with its symbols (functions, types, classes, constants) and line numbers. Use this FIRST to orient yourself; it is far cheaper than reading files.

tools.name: read_file
tools.description: Read a file with numbered lines ("12 | code"). Requires file_path. Search first, then use from_line/to_line (or limit) to read relevant sections rather than entire large files. Use structural inspection when available. NEVER pass search patterns or regex here.

file_path.description: Absolute or project-relative path of the file (or output buffer) to read. Must be a valid file path, NOT a search pattern or regex.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return from from_line.

tools.name: read_file_symbols
tools.description: Get symbols and line ranges from LSP documentSymbol or native Emacs Lisp imenu. Use this before reading a large file to inspect its structure.

file_path.description: Absolute or project-relative path of the file to inspect.

tools.name: read_symbol
tools.description: Read the exact implementation body of a specific symbol (function, method, class, struct, type) by name from a file. Uses LSP/imenu line ranges to fetch only the relevant code without loading the full file.

file_path.description: Absolute or project-relative path of the file.

symbol.description: Name of the symbol (function, method, class, struct, type) to read.

kind.description: Optional symbol kind filter (e.g. Function, Method, Class, Struct, Type).

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load a named skill's instructions. Use when the task matches an available_skills entry.

tools.name: webfetch
tools.description: Fetch a http/https URL and return the response body as text. Use for documentation pages the user named. Do not invent URLs.

tools.name: workspace_grep
tools.description: Search file contents for regex or literal text pattern. ALWAYS use this (or rg/grep) instead of reading entire files when searching for definitions, usages, or text. Uses `rg' (ripgrep) if available, otherwise GNU grep. Read-only, available in all modes.

path.description: File or directory to search (default: project root).

tools.name: write_file
tools.description: Write or rewrite a file completely. Overwrites the entire file with contents (or creates it if it does not exist). Note: for small, localized changes to an existing file, prefer edit_file to save tokens and avoid merge conflicts. Use write_file when replacing the entire file or creating a new file. The human reviews the proposal in ediff before it is saved.

file_path.description: Absolute or project-relative path of the file to write or create.
